newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: GUIDE-REUTERS COVERAGE OF CZECH SENATE ELECTIONS.
newsitem.headline: GUIDE-REUTERS COVERAGE OF CZECH SENATE ELECTIONS.

text.p: The Czech Republic votes on Friday November 15 and Saturday November 16 to elect for the first time an 81-member upper house of parliament, the Senate.
A second round run-off will be held on November 22 and 23 in constituencies where no candidate won more than 50 percent of the vote. This will be between the top two candidates from the first round.
Reuters Prague team is planning in-depth coverage of the final estimates, official results, and reaction to the polls which are the first electoral test of the centre-right minority government.
The first official running results from the first round are expected on Saturday after 1500 local time (1400 GMT) and the final results are expected the same day at about 2100 local time.
The Central Election Committee (UVK) will be releasing results in several waves, each containing data for about 20 constituencies.
There are two news conferences scheduled on Saturday November 16, in which the UVK said it should provide its latest results and other information.
The first starts at 1645 local time and the second, which should bring the final results, is scheduled for 2100 local time.

There will not be any exit-polls but the public TV station CT1 is planning to run a final opinion survey taken on Thursday which legally cannot be released until polls close at 1400 local time on Saturday.
Reuters will carry reports of this final survey.
For the second round, the results should be released fist on November 23 in early afternoon and the final data the same day in the evening.
